active_key.title: Active key
active_key.body: One of the three private keys your Morphit account has. The active key is for moving BLURT — paying listing fees, sending tips, transferring balances. {brand} asks for it (or rather, for the password that unlocks it on your device) only when you're about to spend. It never leaves your browser.

blockchain.title: Blockchain
blockchain.body: A blockchain is a shared record book that thousands of independent computers each keep a full copy of — instead of one company keeping it on a single server. Once something is written in, no single party can quietly erase or rewrite it, because every copy would have to agree to the change. Morphit settles on a blockchain (called Blurt) so your orders, ratings, and messages live somewhere no operator — and no government — can secretly alter or take down. That's what makes Morphit hard to censor or shut off: there's no central database for anyone to seize.

blurt.title: BLURT
blurt.body: BLURT is two things: a blockchain (where Morphit's order ops, fees, and chat ciphertext live), and the asset you pay listing fees with. The asset and the chain share the same name. There is no Morphit token — Morphit uses BLURT directly.

blurt_power.title: BLURT Power (BP)
blurt_power.body: BLURT that you have "powered up" — staked into your account so it can't be spent immediately and it earns you a passive income from staking your BLURT coins. BP gives you weight when voting on Blurt content (separate from Morphit) and is the basis for delegation. Morphit doesn't require any BP; its welcome and loyalty rewards are BP lent to you, which adds to your voting weight.

broadcast.title: Broadcast
broadcast.body: To send a signed operation to the blockchain. Posting an order, cancelling an order, leaving feedback, sending an encrypted chat message — all of these are broadcasts. Once a broadcast lands in a block, it can't be undone (the operation is on-chain forever); only superseded by a later one.

counterparty.title: Counterparty
counterparty.body: The other person in a trade. If you posted a sell order and someone messages you to buy, that person is your counterparty. The word is neutral — it doesn't mean "opponent." Both sides of every Morphit trade have a counterparty: each is the other's.

custom_json.title: custom_json
custom_json.body: A type of operation on the blockchain that carries arbitrary structured data. Morphit's order ops, feedback ops, chat envelopes, and operator registrations are all custom_json operations — they ride on the chain's existing infrastructure rather than requiring a new chain. You don't need to interact with custom_json directly; Morphit builds them for you.

delegation.title: Delegation
delegation.body: Lending some of your BP to another account temporarily, without giving them control of your underlying BLURT. Morphit doesn't require delegation to use, but operators sometimes delegate to new accounts to give them initial weight. Delegations can be undone (with a cooldown period before the BP becomes liquid again).

federation.title: Federation
federation.body: Multiple independent Morphit instances that share the same orderbook and chat ecosystem because they all read from the same underlying blockchain. If one operator goes offline (or hostile), users move to another and find the same orders, the same trades, the same reputations. Federation is what makes Morphit uncensorable.

feedback.title: Feedback
feedback.body: A signed, on-chain rating you leave for a counterparty after a trade. Feedback is permanent — it can't be deleted, only responded to. Your reputation in Morphit is the sum of feedback others have left for you over time. Both sides of every completed trade are entitled to leave one piece of feedback.

fiat.title: Fiat
fiat.body: Government-issued currency: dollars, euros, yen, pesos, rubles. The opposite of crypto. On {brand}, fiat is what changes hands off-platform — you and your counterparty agree on a price in fiat (e.g. USD), settle the fiat side privately (cash, bank transfer, your choice), and {brand} handles only the crypto side.

indexer.title: Indexer
indexer.body: The component of a Morphit instance that watches the chain, decodes Morphit-relevant operations (orders, feedback, chat envelopes), and serves them to the web frontend in a usable shape. The chain is the source of truth; the indexer is just a fast cache. Run by the operator, not by you.

instance.title: Instance
instance.body: A single Morphit website, run by one operator — the site you're on right now is one instance. Because Morphit is federated, many independent instances all read the same blockchain and show the same orders, trades, and reputations. If one instance blocks you or goes offline, you can switch to any other instance and pick up exactly where you left off.

listing_fee.title: Listing fee
listing_fee.body: The small BLURT fee {brand} charges when you post a new order. The fee covers operator costs and disincentivizes spam orderbooks. The first order from a new account is free. Listing fees scale gently with how often you post. Cancelling an order does NOT refund the listing fee — it's the cost of the listing, not the trade.

network_fee.title: Network fee
network_fee.body: Two unrelated things share this name in casual speech: (1) {brand}'s listing fee — the BLURT cost of posting an order; and (2) the Bitcoin or Monero on-chain fee that miners take when you settle the crypto side of a trade. {brand} only ever charges the first; the second is between you and the underlying network when you make the actual transfer.

operator.title: Operator
operator.body: The person or team running a particular Morphit instance — the website you're looking at right now is operated by someone. The operator runs the indexer and relay servers, sets policies for their instance (rate limits, fee tiers, kill-switch), and earns a share of the listing fees that flow through. If an operator goes hostile, you can switch to a different instance and find your same orders, same trades, same reputation.

password.title: Password
password.body: What unlocks your private keys on your device. {brand} never sees, sends, stores, or knows your password — it's used locally by your browser to decrypt the encrypted bundle of keys held in your browser's storage. If you forget your password, the keys are gone; that's why {brand} asks you to write down your seed phrase during onboarding.

permlink.title: Permlink
permlink.body: The unique short identifier of an order on the blockchain — something like `morphit-o-2k4f9`. Permlinks let you (and the chain, and other Morphit instances) refer to a specific order without ambiguity. The order's URL on any Morphit instance ends in its permlink, so order links are portable across instances.

posting_key.title: Posting key
posting_key.body: Another of your account's three private keys. The posting key is for signing content — chat messages, feedback, comments. It's lower-trust than the active key (it can't move BLURT) so a compromise is less catastrophic. Morphit uses it for chat-payload signing and feedback ops; you'll never need to handle it directly.

relay.title: Relay
relay.body: The component of a Morphit instance that handles things the indexer can't — chat envelope acceptance, fee verification, kill-switch enforcement, anti-spam policies. The relay is the moving-parts side of an instance (the indexer is read-only against the chain). Run by the operator, not by you.

release_op.title: Release op
release_op.body: An on-chain operation signed by the @morphit account that announces a new Morphit release: its version, the SHA-256 of its source tarball, and the hashes of the files that start the website. At most once a day your browser reads the newest one from a public Blurt node (a second node only if the first fails) and checks its signature; when the site runs that version, it compares the files it loaded with the signed hashes and warns you if they differ. That catches a file changed by accident or by a partly compromised server — not a hostile operator, who serves the checking code too.

seed_phrase.title: Seed phrase
seed_phrase.body: Twelve English words that, taken together, are the master backup of your account. From the seed phrase your device can re-derive every key your account has. If your device dies and you lose your password, the seed phrase is what gets you back in. Write it down on paper. Don't take a screenshot. Don't email it to yourself. Don't store it in a password manager that lives on the same device.

sign.title: Sign
sign.body: To attach a cryptographic signature to a piece of data using one of your private keys, proving the data came from you and hasn't been altered. When {brand} asks you to "unlock to sign," it's about to ask the chain to accept an action on your behalf — posting an order, sending a message, paying a fee. The signing happens locally on your device; the private key never leaves.

glossary.heading: Glossary
glossary.intro: Plain-language explanations of the words {brand} uses. If a term in the UI is confusing, it should be defined here. If it isn't, please file an issue report.
glossary.footnote: These definitions are deliberately short. For longer or more technical answers, see the {faqOpen}FAQ{faqClose}.

aead.title: AEAD
aead.body: Authenticated encryption: it both encrypts the message and detects any tampering, in a single step.

dns.title: DNS
dns.body: Domain Name System: the internet's directory that turns a name like morphit.io into a server address.

ecdh.title: ECDH
ecdh.body: Elliptic-Curve Diffie–Hellman: a method for two parties to derive a shared secret without ever sending it.

ecies.title: ECIES
ecies.body: A standard scheme for encrypting a message to someone's public key, so only the holder of the matching private key can read it.

ens.title: ENS
ens.body: Ethereum Name Service: maps readable names like yourbrand.eth to decentralized website content.

ipfs.title: IPFS
ipfs.body: InterPlanetary File System: a peer-to-peer network that serves files by their content hash instead of a server address.

mcp.title: MCP
mcp.body: Model Context Protocol: an open standard that lets AI assistants read data through well-defined tools.

p2p.title: P2P
p2p.body: Peer-to-peer: participants connect and transact directly, with no central server or middleman.

pwa.title: PWA
pwa.body: Progressive Web App: a website you can install and use like a native app, even offline.

rss.title: RSS
rss.body: A standard web-feed format for subscribing to a site's updates — here, {brand}'s live order feed.

tls.title: TLS
tls.body: Transport Layer Security: the encryption that protects data in transit — the 'S' in HTTPS.

x25519.title: X25519
x25519.body: A fast, modern elliptic curve used for key agreement: two sides compute a shared secret from each other's public keys.

home.hero_title: Anonymously trade cryptocurrencies, fiat, goods, services and more
home.hero_body: {brand} connects buyers and sellers directly. No KYC, non-custodial, no cookies, E2EE, no tracking, no escrow, private by default, open source, fully-distributed

privacy.title: Privacy first
privacy.body: No KYC, email, phone/SMS, cookies, analytics or selfies. Pick a cool username, that's it, seriously.

true_p2p.title: True P2P
true_p2p.body: Assets move directly between Buyer and Seller only. No exchange wallet, escrow, arbitrators or middleman.

unstoppable.title: Unstoppable by design
unstoppable.body: Reachable on clearnet, Tor, Lokinet, I2P, ENS and Federated instance runners. Block one and many others remain.

discoverability.title: Discoverability
discoverability.body: Federation uses an open public blockchain and RSS for orderbook distribution, trade finalization and user reputation.

encrypted_chat.title: Encrypted Chat
encrypted_chat.body: Buyer/Seller conversations are 100% private, E2EE and immutable for posterity in case you have a future dispute.

reputation.title: Reputation is everything
reputation.body: Use any number of different websites and your good reputation follows you. Your personal trades are always there.

trade_anything.title: Trade anything
trade_anything.body: 16+ cryptos plus direct goods, services and even barter. Cross-asset, cross-network, cross-medium.

home.run_node_body: Your brand, your users, and 90% of the BLURT listing fees paid on your site, straight to your account on chain within seconds. Featured-slot bids and first-message fees on your site pay you 90% too. One command installs everything on a small server or an old laptop.

identity.streaming_link_aria: Visit this user's streaming profile (opens in new tab)
identity.website_link_aria: Visit this user's website (opens in new tab)

banner.heading: Install {brand}
banner.blurb: Add it to your device for a faster, full-screen experience.
banner.ios_help: In Safari, tap the Share button, then "Add to Home Screen".

instances.title: Known Morphit instances
instances.intro: Morphit is federated. Independent Operators run Morphit instances, and they get paid 90% of all of the BLURT listing fees on their sites. The more people that use their site, the more they get paid. Learn more about it in the [FAQ], or [download] Morphit to your server now to [run your own node].
instances.bookmark_tip: 💡 Tip: bookmark a few of these instances — and their Tor, I2P, Lokinet or ENS addresses. The orderbook lives on the public blockchain. So if any one site is ever inaccessible, you can reach the very same orders and trades in many other places.
instances.add_yours_body: Run a Morphit instance? Just register on-chain — every other Morphit indexer will discover you automatically. The wizard (morphit-ops init) handles registration during first-time setup.

status_desc.good: Reachable, healthy, and synced within the lag threshold.
status_desc.quiet: Healthy, but no orderbook activity in the last 7 days.
status_desc.syncing: Reachable and healthy, but still catching up to the chain. Turns Good once synced.
status_desc.stale: Reachable, but its health check is degraded — a real problem on that instance.
status_desc.unreachable: Couldn't be reached over the network on the last check.
status_desc.clearnet_blocked: Alive on-chain and reachable over Tor, but its public web address is blocked from outside its country. Not down — censored.
status_desc.mismatch: Reachable, but its operator account or treasury addresses don't match the canonical chain values.
status_desc.never: Queued — the probe hasn't checked this instance yet.

instances.empty_body: Your indexer is still catching up to chain head, or no operators have registered with an origin yet. Check back later.
instances.no_match_body: No instances currently have this status — try a different filter.

login.title: Sign in to {brand}
login.body: Pick the option that matches how you got here.
login.no_account_body: Create a new account above by just picking a cool username, that's literally all there is to it.
login.import_existing: Sign in with a 12-word seed, json keyfile or posting key

unlock.wrong_password: That password does not match your keystore. Try again, or use your seed phrase to sign in.
unlock.no_keystore: No keystore found on this device. Please sign in with your seed phrase or create a new account.

phase.requesting: Choose your YubiKey from the browser prompt…

error.enroll_verify_failed: Couldn't verify your YubiKey. Re-enroll it in Settings, then try again.
error.webhid_unsupported: Your browser doesn't support hardware keys. Try Chrome, Edge, or Brave.
error.open_failed: Couldn't open the YubiKey. Make sure it's plugged in.
error.timeout: YubiKey timed out. Try again and tap promptly when prompted.
error.unknown: YubiKey unlock failed. Try again, or use your seed phrase to enter.
error.protocol_violation: Your YubiKey returned a malformed response. Try a different USB port, cable, or YubiKey.
error.unsafe_kdf_params: Your saved keystore appears to have been altered (security parameters don't meet the safe minimum). Restore from your seed phrase.
error.wrap_schema_unsupported: Your saved keystore uses a format this version of Morphit doesn't understand. Update Morphit and try again.
error.unwrap_failed: Couldn't decrypt your keystore with that YubiKey. Make sure you tapped the right key.
error.label_too_long: Saved keystore has invalid label data. Restore from your seed phrase.
error.wrap_limit_reached: Saved keystore is in an unexpected state. Restore from your seed phrase.
error.duplicate_yubikey_label: Saved keystore has duplicate YubiKey labels. Restore from your seed phrase.
error.not_layered: This keystore has no YubiKey enrolled. Use your password to unlock instead.
error.no_yubikey_wrap: This keystore has no YubiKey enrolled. Use your password to unlock instead.
error.wrap_index_out_of_range: Saved keystore references a YubiKey wrap that isn't there. Restore from your seed phrase.
error.cannot_unenroll_last_wrap: This shouldn't happen at unlock — please report it.

yubikey.totp_then_tap: Enter the code, then unlock with your YubiKey again — it asks for a touch, then one more.

unlock.envelope_corrupt: Your stored keystore appears damaged. Re-import from your seed or keyfile.
unlock.yubikey_required: This keystore is locked to a hardware key. Use Unlock with YubiKey.
unlock.unsupported_envelope: This keystore was created by a newer version of Morphit. Update before unlocking.
unlock.generic_error: Unable to unlock right now. Try again, or sign in with your seed.

welcome_back.title: Welcome back
welcome_back.body: Unlock your encrypted keystore with the password you set up.
welcome_back.alternatives_body: No password reset — {brand} is non-custodial and nobody can recover it. But if you wrote down your 12-word seed phrase, you can still sign in with that.
welcome_back.yubikey_only_body: This keystore is locked to a YubiKey. Plug yours in and tap to unlock.
welcome_back.yubikey_browser_unsupported: YubiKey unlock requires Chrome, Edge, Brave, or another Chromium browser. You can also use your seed phrase to enter.

login.qr_pair_cta: Sign in with your phone via QR

signout_before_switch_modal.title: Sign out
signout_before_switch_modal.body: Signing in to a different account will sign you out of your @{account} account first. OK?

login_qr.title: Sign in with your phone
login_qr.subtitle: Scan this code with the {brand} app on your phone. Your keys never leave the phone.
login_qr.readonly_body: QR pairing signs you in on this device for browsing, profile, and chat history. Posts, messages, and other actions are signed on your phone — that's why your keys never leave it.
login_qr.starting: Setting up a one-time login code…
login_qr.qr_render_error: Couldn't render the code. Refresh the page.
login_qr.qr_aria: QR code containing a one-time login request
login_qr.scan_instruction: On your phone, tap your avatar (top-right) and choose "Sign in to another device", then point its camera at this code.
login_qr.no_phone_scanner_body: You don't need a separate QR app — {brand} has its own scanner. On your phone, tap your avatar (top-right) and choose "Sign in to another device".
login_qr.received_body: Welcome, @{account}. Taking you to the orderbook…
login_qr.expired_body: Codes only work for 5 minutes. Tap below for a fresh one.
login_qr.rejected_body: Something didn't match up. Tap below to try a fresh code.

mailing_address_modal.heading: Share your mailing address
mailing_address_modal.intro: Share a physical address with your trade partner so they can ship goods or mail cash. Stays in this encrypted chat only.
mailing_address_modal.privacy_e2ee: This address is end-to-end encrypted in chat — only you and your trade partner can read it.
mailing_address_modal.privacy_irreversible: Sharing is irreversible: once sent, your partner has your address even if you clear the message later.
mailing_address_modal.privacy_pobox_tip: Consider using a P.O. box, mail-drop service, or virtual mailbox instead of your home address.
mailing_address_modal.privacy_clear_chat: After the trade completes, consider clearing this conversation history on both ends.
mailing_address_modal.country_help: Two-letter ISO country code (e.g. US, DE, JP).
mailing_address_modal.recipient_help: Name on the mailbox or package. Leave blank for anonymous P.O. boxes.

problem.country_invalid: Pick a country, or type its 2-letter code (for example MX).
problem.street_too_long: The street address is too long (at most 200 characters).
problem.city_too_long: The city is too long (at most 100 characters).
problem.postal_code_length: Enter the postal code (at most 20 characters).
problem.street2_too_long: The second address line is too long (at most 200 characters).
problem.state_too_long: The state or region is too long (at most 100 characters).
problem.recipient_name_too_long: The recipient name is too long (at most 100 characters).
problem.note_too_long: The note is too long (at most 500 characters).
problem.note_forbidden_chars: The note contains a tab, line break or another invisible control character. Remove it and try again.
problem.order_permlink_invalid: This address can't be linked to the order. Close this window and open it again from the order.

mailing_address_modal.send_failed: The address could not be sent. Check your connection and try again.

error.load_failed: Couldn't load your balance. The blockchain may be slow or down.
error.export_failed: Couldn't export PnL data. Try again.
error.export_too_much_history: This account has more activity in the last year than the export can read (over 50,000 blockchain entries), so no file was made rather than an incomplete one.
error.export_busy: The server is busy reading account histories right now, so no file was made. Try again in a minute.

my_orders.heading: Your orders
my_orders.subtitle: Every order you've posted on {brand}.
my_orders.empty_body: When you're ready, posting an order takes about a minute.
my_orders.empty_category: No orders are in this category.
my_orders.error_body: The indexer didn't respond. Try again in a moment.

order.fee_reused: Not in orderbook — payment already used
order.fee_missing: Not in orderbook — fee payment not received
order.viewed_tooltip: Approximate count of times this offer has been viewed. Visible only to you.
order.action_relist_hint: Pre-fills the form for you with the original values and terms.
order.feedback_no_counterparty: No chats with a counterparty have happened yet
order.feature_arming_hint: Available the moment your order is live
order.fee_proof_unsupported: Not in orderbook — fee can't be checked; post again with the transaction key

cancel.confirm_body: This removes your order from the orderbook, so no one new can respond to it — and it can't be undone. Any chats you've already started stay open, and no one is charged. If you paid a listing fee, it isn't refunded.

my_orders.view_on_explorer: View my account on the block explorer

next_steps.heading: What's next
next_steps.browse_body: See what other traders are offering. Find a deal that matches what you want.
next_steps.post_body: Tell the network what you're trading. The first one is free — no listing fee.
next_steps.walkthrough_body: A 5-minute explainer of how a Morphit trade actually works, start to finish.

error.load_failed: Couldn't load your orders. Try again.
error.no_account: Sign in with your account to see your orders.

no_account.title: Set up to see your orders
no_account.body: Your orders are stored on-chain under your Morphit identity. Create one to start trading, or unlock an existing identity to view your history.

locked.title: Unlock to view your orders
locked.body: Your order history stays behind your unlock, so a locked device never reveals your trades. Enter your password to view it.

fee_status_banner.heading: Fee status
fee_status_banner.body: 💡 Each order below shows its listing-fee status. An order appears in the public orderbook only once its fee is verified — a badge reading “not received”, “underpaid” or “not yet verified” is why an order may appear to be missing.

complete.confirm_body: This confirms the trade is finished and removes the order from the public orderbook. It can't be undone.

nav.start_hint: sign in or create an account

onboarding.title: Let's set up your keys
onboarding.intro: Your Morphit account is a pair of cryptographic keys. They are made right here on your device and never leave it. If you lose them, no one can recover them — not even us. That's the price of true privacy.

path_reputation.title: Create a new identity
path_reputation.cta_hint: New keys, made on this device
path_reputation.body: Your successful trades build a public track record that helps people trust you. Every trade of one account is publicly linked to it — for unlinked trades, use a separate account.

onboarding.generating: Generating your keys securely on your device…
onboarding.generated_body: Before you do anything else, back them up. If you lose them, your account is gone forever. We warned you — this is the tradeoff for keys only you control.
onboarding.this_is_you: This is how you appear to others (unless you change it later)

backup.title: Back up your keys
backup.seed_hint: 12 words. In order. On paper. In KeePass(.info). Make a backup copy too. Store the 12 words somewhere SAFE. Do not photograph them. Do not email them to yourself.
backup.confirm_wrote_down: I wrote the seed down on paper
backup.confirm_understand: I'll keep these 12 words safe — I know they're the only way back into my account.
backup.password_hint: Choose a strong passphrase. This encrypts the backup file — not the keys on {brand}.
backup.continue: I've backed up my keys — continue
backup.blocked: Please confirm both boxes before continuing.
backup.password_too_short: Password must be at least 10 characters.
backup.keyfile_explain: Optionally download an encrypted backup of your keys. Same password as above. Store the file somewhere safe (USB drive, cloud you trust, another device) as an alternate path back into your account if the browser storage is wiped.
backup.password_strength_common: This password is among the most common — pick something unique to you.
backup.password_strength_trivial: Sequential or repeated patterns are easy to guess. Mix it up.
backup.persist_failed: Couldn't save your encrypted keystore to this device. Storage may be unavailable. Choose 'Seed every time' instead, or try again.
backup.password_strength_too_simple: Mix in numbers, symbols, or uppercase — or make it 12+ characters.

print_card.aria: Print a paper backup card with your 12 words
print_card.helper_hint: Opens your browser's print dialog. You can print to paper or save as PDF.
print_card.title: My Morphit backup card
print_card.subtitle: Keep this paper safe — it is the only way back into your account.
print_card.warning_body: Anyone who finds these 12 words can take everything in your Morphit account. Store this paper somewhere only you can reach — a safe, a locked drawer, or a secure deposit box. Don't photograph it. Don't email it. Don't store it in cloud notes.
print_card.instructions: If you ever lose access to your device, type these 12 words into Morphit's import flow on a new device to recover your account.

backup.keys_intro: These let you use this account in other Blurt apps. Your 12 words are still your main backup.

import.title: Import existing keys
import.body: Already have a Blurt account? Pick how you have your key stored. If you've never used Blurt before, [[go back]] and create a new account instead.
import.seed_hint: For users who set up Morphit (or another wallet that ships our seed format) before. If you don't have a 12-word seed, use one of the other tabs.
import.keyfile_hint: An encrypted .json file you exported from Morphit on another device, or a backup you saved.

posting_only.warning_body: If you don't have a 12-word seed or a Keyfile, just paste your Posting Key here instead. We'll encrypt it on this device for you. You'll be able to read, post, and trade with others, but NOT get discounted listing fees.
posting_only.wif_hint: Starts with a 5. Never shared with the operator — encrypted on this device only.
posting_only.new_password_hint: Choose a strong password. At least 8 characters. Used to unlock {brand} on this device. Not your Blurt password.

error.passwords_mismatch: Passwords don't match. Please retype both.
error.account_not_found: We detected your account (@{account}) but couldn't load it from Blurt just now. Check your connection and try again.
error.key_not_on_account: This is a valid Blurt key, but it doesn't belong to '@{account}'. Double-check the username above, or paste the Posting key that matches this account.

wif.too-short: That WIF is too short to be a valid Blurt key.
wif.too-long: That WIF is too long to be a valid Blurt key.
wif.bad-charset: WIF contains unexpected characters. WIFs use Base58 (no 0, O, I, or l).
wif.bad-version: That doesn't look like a Blurt private key.
wif.bad-checksum: WIF checksum failed — there's a typo somewhere. Re-copy and try again.
wif.bad-length: WIF is the wrong length to be a valid Blurt key.
wif.bad-scalar: Decoded successfully but the key is mathematically invalid. Re-copy and try again.

wrong_role.active: That's your Active key, which controls funds and account changes. For your safety, {brand} signs in with your Posting key only. Please paste your Posting key instead.
wrong_role.owner: That's your Owner key — the most powerful key on your account, and the one to guard most carefully. {brand} only ever signs you in with your Posting key. Please paste your Posting key instead.
wrong_role.memo: That's your Memo key — it's only used to encrypt and decrypt private messages and can't sign you in. Please paste your Posting key instead.

error.could_not_resolve: We couldn't detect your account from this key. Double-check that you copied your Posting Private Key correctly, or import with your 12-word seed or Keyfile instead.

posting_only.manual_account_hint: We couldn't detect your account from this key — it may be from before Blurt existed. Type your Blurt username so we can confirm the key belongs to it.
posting_only.manual_account_invalid: That username doesn't match this key. Check the spelling, or that you pasted the right Posting Private Key.
posting_only.detected_account: Recognised — this key belongs to @{account}. No username needed.

error.seed_word_count: A Blurt seed phrase is exactly 12 words — you've entered {count}. Make sure all 12 are present, each separated by a single space.
error.seed_invalid: That seed phrase isn't valid — one or more words aren't from the standard seed word list, or a word was mistyped. Check each word carefully and try again.
error.keyfile_password_wrong: That password doesn't match this keyfile. Passwords are case-sensitive, so check Caps Lock and any stray spaces, then try again.
error.keyfile_corrupt: This file isn't a valid Morphit keyfile, or it's been damaged. Upload the 'morphit-keyfile-….json' file you saved when you created your account — not a screenshot or a different file.
error.generic: Something unexpected went wrong while signing you in — it wasn't your key or password. Please wait a moment and try again.
error.network: We couldn't reach the Blurt network to verify your key. This is a connection problem on the network side, not a problem with your key. Check your internet and try again in a moment.
error.keyfile_too_large: This file is far larger than any Morphit keyfile, so it is not one. Upload the 'morphit-keyfile-….json' file you saved.
error.keyfile_too_new: This keyfile was made by a newer version of Morphit than this site runs. Open it on an up-to-date Morphit site, or use your seed phrase here.
error.keyfile_totp_required: The password is right. This keyfile also has two-factor authentication: enter the code from your authenticator app (or a backup code) below, then sign in again.
error.keyfile_yubikey_only: This keyfile opens only with its YubiKey, and importing such a keyfile is not supported. Unlock it where the YubiKey was set up, or use your seed phrase here.

remember_me.heading: You're signed in — one more choice
remember_me.body: Your keys are loaded for this browser session. By default, when you close this tab the keys disappear and you'll need your 12-word seed phrase again next time. If this is your own computer, you can choose to remember you on this device behind a password instead.
remember_me.checkbox_label: Automatically remember me on this device? (assuming nobody else uses it)
remember_me.password_intro: Pick a password for this device. It'll be required to unlock {brand} next time you visit. The password stays on this device — {brand} never sees it.
remember_me.password_hint: Choose a strong password. At least 8 characters. Used to unlock {brand} on this device.
remember_me.password_strength_too_simple: Too simple. Use a longer or less predictable password.
remember_me.password_strength_common: This password appears on common-password lists. Pick something less guessable.
remember_me.submit_session_only: Skip — keep me signed in just for this session

error.password_weak: Password is too weak. Use something longer or less predictable.

remember_me.body_password_set: Your keys are loaded for this browser session. By default, when you close this tab they disappear and you'll need to sign in again next time. If this is your own computer, you can choose to be remembered on this device — you'll unlock next time with the same password you just used.

confirm.title: Let's confirm you wrote it down
confirm.body: Type a few specific words from the seed you just saved. This makes sure you really have the phrase written down, not just that you clicked a box.
confirm.wrong: That's not quite right. Double-check your written copy of the seed.

register_name.title: Choose your account name
register_name.subtitle: This is the name people see when they trade with you. It's permanent — choose something you're happy to use for a long time.
register_name.field_hint: 3–16 lowercase letters, digits, or dashes. Must start with a letter. No spaces, no dots, no capitals.

availability.taken: That name is already taken. Pick another.
availability.rejected_generic: That name isn't allowed. Try a different one.
availability.unreachable: Can't reach the registration service right now. Check your connection or try again in a moment.

reasons.must_start_with_letter: Must start with a lowercase letter.
reasons.bad_chars: Only lowercase letters, digits, and dashes are allowed.
reasons.consecutive_dashes: Two dashes in a row are not allowed.
reasons.leading_trailing_dash: The name can't start or end with a dash.
reasons.reserved: That name is reserved. Pick another.
reasons.rate_limited: Too many checks in a short time. Wait a minute and try again.

fee.title: Registration is free for you
fee.hint: Account creation is free — {brand} covers the network cost.
fee.body: We pay the on-chain creation fee — you don't need any BLURT to sign up.

errors.local_key_error: Something went wrong with your keys locally. Try refreshing and starting onboarding again.
errors.already_registered: That name was just taken by someone else. Pick another.
errors.name_not_allowed: That name isn't allowed. Try a different one.
errors.invalid_pubkey: Your keys were rejected by the chain. Please refresh and start onboarding again.
errors.rate_limited: You've made too many attempts. Try again in an hour.
errors.relay_out_of_funds: Our registration service is temporarily out of funds. Please try again later, or skip for now and register when you're ready to trade.
errors.chain_unavailable: Can't reach the network right now. Try again in a moment.
errors.duplicate_submission: It looks like the same claim is already in flight. Please wait a minute.
errors.broadcast_failed: Registration was rejected. Try a different name, or skip for now.
errors.unreachable: Can't reach the registration service. Check your connection and try again.
errors.rate_limited_daily: You've reached today's signup limit. Please try again tomorrow.
errors.spacing_cooldown: You recently created an account. Please wait {minutes} more minute{minutes, plural, one {} other {s}} before creating another.
errors.signups_disabled: Signups are temporarily unavailable on this instance. Please try another Morphit mirror or check back later.
errors.daily_ceiling_reached: This instance has reached its daily signup limit. Please try again tomorrow or try another Morphit mirror.
errors.invite_problem: Your signup token expired or was already used. Please try again.
errors.altcha_problem: Human verification failed. Please try again.
errors.daily_ceiling_voucher_intro: If you don't want to wait or hop instances, here's a fast path: get a voucher code from the Agorise community and create your account on a different service, then come back here to log in.
errors.daily_ceiling_voucher_step_1: Join us in the Agorise Matrix room {matrix_open}#agorise:matrix.org{matrix_close}. A community member will give you a voucher code.
errors.daily_ceiling_voucher_step_2: Open {plugin_open}blurtplugin.online/account{plugin_close}, paste your voucher code, and create your account there.
errors.daily_ceiling_voucher_step_3: Come back to {brand} and log in with the keys you just generated. You're trading.
errors.name_high_value: That name is reserved for legitimate-claim review (it's short, a brand, or a common dictionary word). Try a longer or more personal name. If you have a legitimate claim to this exact name, contact the operator.
errors.name_sequential_pattern: Recent account creations from your network have followed a sequential pattern that suggests automation. Try a name that doesn't share a prefix with recent signups, or wait an hour and retry.
errors.daily_ceiling_voucher_external_warning: blurtplugin.online is a Blurt-community service, not run by {brand}. You're leaving {brand} when you click. If the link doesn't work, type the URL by hand:
errors.relay_fee_spike: Registration is paused on this server while its operator reviews a change in the Blurt account fee. Please try again later, or skip for now.
errors.broadcast_outcome_unknown: The Blurt network did not confirm in time whether your account was created. Wait a minute and try again with the same name — if it was created, you will be told so.

success.title: Welcome to {brand}
success.body: @{name} — your account is now live and ready for trading!

leave_guard.title: Wait — are you sure that you want to leave this page right now?
leave_guard.body: Your new username has not been registered yet.

register_name.have_account_link: Already have a Blurt account? Enter it in Settings

unlock_mode.heading: How do you want to unlock next time?
unlock_mode.explain: Your keys live on this device for this session. Pick how you want to get back in after you close the tab.
unlock_mode.password_body: Set a password. Your encrypted keystore stays on this device, and you can unlock with just the password next visit — no 12-word seed phrase needed. You can also use Lock Session from the avatar menu without losing your data. Choose this for your own personal computer.
unlock_mode.seed_only_body: Nothing is stored on this device. Every new session starts with you re-entering your 12-word seed phrase. Most private — no encrypted keystore to attack, no data to wipe on public computers. Choose this for public or shared devices, or if you'd rather trade a little convenience for maximum privacy.
unlock_mode.must_choose: Choose an unlock method before continuing.

leave_confirm.title: Leave onboarding?
leave_confirm.body: Leaving this page will discard the keys you just generated. If you haven't written down the seed, you can't recover this identity.

paths.heading: How do you want to start?

error.generate_failed: Couldn't generate new keys. Try refreshing the page.
error.keyfile_download_failed: Couldn't prepare your keyfile for download. Try again.
error.quiz_submit_failed: Couldn't continue past the quiz. Try again.
error.keys_reveal_failed: Couldn't show your keys just now. Please try again.

back_confirm.title: Discard this seed and start over?
back_confirm.body: Going back will discard the seed phrase you just generated. The 12 words will be wiped from this device. If you've already written them down somewhere, you'll want to destroy that copy too — it won't unlock anything anymore.

banner.title: Your posts are blocked on this instance
banner.body: @{operator}, the operator of this instance, blocked your account on {since}. This is a curation choice by THIS instance — your funds, identity, and chain history are unaffected, and other Morphit instances are not.
banner.no_reason_provided: The operator did not provide a reason.
banner.still_visible_elsewhere: Your posts are blocked only on this instance — they’re still visible on every other Morphit instance.
banner.contact_prefix: If you think this is a mistake, you can reach the community on Matrix:
banner.what_it_does_not_do: What this block does NOT do
banner.not_funds: It does not touch your BLURT, BTC, XMR, or any other funds — they are in your control.
banner.not_other_instances: It does not follow you to other Morphit instances. You can sign in elsewhere unaffected.
banner.not_chain: It is not a chain-level ban. Your account remains on Blurt with full posting rights.
banner.reversible: It can be reversed by the operator at any time.
banner.does_filter_listings: Your trade listings are hidden from this instance's orderbook view.

operators.title: Morphit operators
operators.subtitle: All public Morphit {link} are run by independent operators. Pick one, or run your own.
operators.empty_body: No additional operators have registered with the chain yet. Anyone can start earning their 90% share of BLURT-paid listing fees. If you'd like to be among the first independent operators, start here.

order_detail.not_found_body: This order doesn't exist. The link may be wrong, or the order was removed.
order_detail.error_body: Something went wrong reaching the indexer. Please try again in a moment.
order_detail.fee_reused: Fee already used by another listing
order_detail.cta_hint: Interested in this trade? Use the Message button above to coordinate payment details with the poster. Settlement happens directly between you — {brand} never holds funds.

pay_zec.description: Zcash: launched 2016, zk-SNARK shielded transactions (Sapling + Orchard pools) plus transparent addresses (t1/t3, like Bitcoin). Fair-launched with a founders-reward halving schedule. Per-trade, recipients pick the address type that matches their posture. Trade-only on {brand} — cannot pay listing fees.

pay_arrr.description: Pay in Pirate Chain (ARRR).  Pirate Chain is a proof-of-work cryptocurrency that ships chain-level shielded transactions via the Sapling zk-SNARK pool — sender, recipient, and amount are hidden on-chain by construction.  Single address format (zs1 Sapling shielded).  Use a Pirate Chain wallet like Treasure Chest, Pirate.Black, or the Verus-integrated Pirate wallet.

pay_dcr.description: Pay in Decred (DCR).  Decred is a hybrid Proof-of-Work + Proof-of-Stake cryptocurrency with on-chain governance via Politeia.  Two receive-address formats: Ds (P2PKH) and Dc (P2SH).  Use a Decred wallet like dcrwallet, Decrediton, or Cake Wallet.

pay_sol.description: Pay in Solana (SOL).  Solana is a high-throughput Proof-of-Stake cryptocurrency.  Use a Solana wallet like Phantom, Solflare, or Cake Wallet for SOL.  Send native SOL — not wrapped SOL (wSOL) or SPL tokens.

pay_eth.description: Pay in Ethereum (ETH).  Ethereum is a Proof-of-Stake cryptocurrency.  Use an Ethereum wallet like MetaMask, Rabby, or Rainbow.  Send native ETH — not wrapped ETH (WETH) or ERC-20 tokens.

pay_xrp.description: Pay in Ripple (XRP). XRP is a Federated Byzantine Agreement cryptocurrency on the XRP Ledger. Use an XRPL wallet like Xaman (formerly Xumm), Crossmark, or Bifrost. Send native XRP. {brand} carries no destination tag, so the seller must share a self-custody XRPL address that needs none — never an exchange deposit address.

plan.heading: What we're building
plan.subtitle: The plan is public. We ship in phases so every piece is done well.
plan.phase_1_body: The shell, the ten languages, the keygen flow, the searchable help — everything a first-time visitor needs, without any server-side account.
plan.phase_2_body: Connect to the chain. Ship the relay service that broadcasts user-signed operations. Release-discovery pointer lands on-chain.
plan.phase_3_body: Indexer goes live. Browse, filter, and post orders. 15-minute replace window. Sybil-resistant fee escalation. Self-trade detection.
plan.phase_4_body: End-to-end encrypted chat. Signed feedback with buyer/seller roles. Public reputation profiles.
plan.phase_5_body: Live BTC / XMR / BLURT payment flows. Tor, Lokinet, and I2P hidden services. IPFS release mirror. PWA + Federated instances onboarding.
plan.phase_6_body: Developers can embed a scoped orderbook screen into their UI. Users can search/browse/respond to offers without leaving the UI they trust.

asset_explainer.btc: Bitcoin (BTC) — the original cryptocurrency, used worldwide. Public ledger; transactions are visible. Network fees and confirmation time vary with network demand.
asset_explainer.xmr: Monero (XMR) — privacy-first cryptocurrency. Hides amounts, balances, senders and recipients by default. Ideal if privacy matters to you.
asset_explainer.blurt: BLURT — the social blockchain Morphit runs on. Fast (3-second blocks), zero-fee transfers, built-in rewards system. Perfect for reputation-building, trade posterity and connecting with like-minded people.
asset_explainer.usdt: Tether (USDT) — a stablecoin pegged 1:1 to USD. Centrally controlled — Tether Inc. can freeze any address.
asset_explainer.bch: Bitcoin Cash (BCH). Forked from Bitcoin in 2017 to favor bigger blocks and lower per-transaction fees over fee-market dynamics. Transparent ledger like BTC; no issuer can freeze addresses. Trade-only on {brand} — listing fees still paid in BLURT, BTC, or XMR.
asset_explainer.ltc: Litecoin (LTC). Forked from Bitcoin in 2011 with faster 2.5-minute blocks and Scrypt mining. Transparent like Bitcoin — every transaction is publicly visible on the chain. No central issuer; nobody can freeze your addresses.
asset_explainer.dash: Dash (DASH). Forked from Litecoin in 2014 with masternode-coordinated services. Transparent at the base layer like Bitcoin — every transaction is publicly visible on the chain. No central issuer; nobody can freeze your addresses. Optional PrivateSend mixing (a CoinJoin variant coordinated by masternodes) provides opt-in privacy.
asset_explainer.usdc: USD Coin (USDC) — a stablecoin pegged 1:1 to USD, issued by Circle. Centrally controlled — Circle can freeze any address.
asset_explainer.dai: DAI is a USD-pegged stablecoin by MakerDAO. More decentralized than USDT/USDC at the contract level (no admin freeze) but partly backed by USDC via the Peg Stability Module.
asset_explainer.doge: Dogecoin (DOGE). Launched 2013 as a fair-launch fork of Lucky Coin (itself a Litecoin fork). Transparent at the base layer like Bitcoin — every transaction is publicly visible on the chain. No central issuer; nobody can freeze your addresses. Merge-mined with Litecoin since 2014 (auxiliary proof-of-work).
asset_explainer.zec: Zcash (ZEC). Launched 2016 as the first practical deployment of zero-knowledge proofs in a cryptocurrency. Transparent and shielded address types coexist on the same chain — t1/t3 addresses are publicly visible like Bitcoin's legacy addresses, while zs1 (Sapling) and u1 (Unified Address with Orchard receivers) use zk-SNARKs to hide sender, recipient, and amount. Choose the address type that matches your trade's privacy posture.
asset_explainer.arrr: Pirate Chain (ARRR) — chain-level shielded transactions via the Sapling zk-SNARK pool; every transfer is private by construction. Single address format (zs1 Sapling, bech32, 78 chars). Trade-only on {brand}; listing fees stay BLURT/BTC/XMR.
asset_explainer.dcr: Decred (DCR). A coin whose community votes on how the project is run. Its public ledger is visible like Bitcoin's, and its wallet has an optional privacy mode. No central issuer — nobody can freeze your coins.
asset_explainer.sol: Solana (SOL) — high-throughput Proof-of-Stake cryptocurrency. Native SOL transfer (not wrapped SOL or SPL tokens). 32-44 character base58 addresses (same shape as USDT-Solana and USDC-Solana addresses; asset field disambiguates).
asset_explainer.eth: Ethereum (ETH) — Proof-of-Stake cryptocurrency. Native ETH transfer (not wrapped ETH or ERC-20 tokens). 42-character 0x-prefixed hex addresses (same shape as USDT-ERC20, USDC-ERC20, DAI-ERC20, and every EVM token-account address; asset field + network field disambiguate).
asset_explainer.xrp: Ripple (XRP) — Federated Byzantine Agreement cryptocurrency on the XRP Ledger. 24-34 character base58 addresses starting with `r`. Destination tags (32-bit integers) are required when sending to exchange-hosted addresses — your peer-to-peer counterparty typically does not need one. XRPL accounts need ≥1 XRP base reserve to exist.
asset_explainer.barter: Barter (goods/services). Not a cryptocurrency — you offer wares or a service and get paid in the crypto(s) you choose to accept. Price it in your local currency; you and the buyer work out the details in chat and settle in one of your accepted cryptos. Describe exactly what you're offering in the Terms field.

form.waiver_fiat_hint: 💡 Most BLURT trades on Morphit happen with active Blurt social-network users, existing operators, or via barter. So, pick the fiat denomination that you use locally (USD, EUR, MXN, etc), and offer In-Person or Barter (goods/services) payment methods on Step 3 if you want to offer something else of value.

fee.heading: Listing fee
fee.tier_label_high: Heavy-poster tier — fees increase with usage
fee.explainer: A small fee discourages spam by making it costly to flood the orderbook with junk listings.

submit.review_hint: Once posted, you get 15 minutes to fix any typos. You can also Cancel and Re-list if you need to.

success.title: Your order is live!
success.body: It'll appear in the orderbook in under 1 minute.
success.waiver_title: Your free first order is live!
success.waiver_body: It's already broadcast to the blockchain and visible in the orderbook to everyone — Morphit covered the listing fee for you. ❤️
success.waiver_step_1: Someone interested in trading BLURT for what you're offering will message you. You'll see a notification on the chat icon in the header — keep an eye out.
success.waiver_step_2: Chat to confirm terms (price, payment timing, location). When you're ready, share your BLURT receiving address (use the address-share button in the chat); they send you BLURT, you send them whatever you agreed to in return.
success.waiver_step_3: Once both sides confirm receipt, leave each other star-rating feedback. That feedback is permanent and builds your reputation. Your 10 BLURT + 10 BLURT Power welcome bonus comes with your first completed trade on a listing you paid for.
success.feature_upsell_heading: Want more eyes on this listing?
success.feature_upsell_body: Bid for a featured slot to put your order at the top of the orderbook for a few hours. The minimum bid is 6 hours; the rate is set per-instance. Most operators ship 50 BLURT/hour as the default.
success.edit_window_tooltip: Edits are only possible within 15 minutes of posting. After that, cancel and re-post.
success.btc_title: Posted! One step left: pay the fee
success.btc_body: Your order goes on the orderbook by itself as soon as its Bitcoin fee is paid and confirmed.

broadcast_error.title: The order didn't go through
broadcast_error.body_generic: The chain didn't accept your broadcast. Nothing was paid. Try again or check your connection.
broadcast_error.body_insufficient_funds: Your account doesn't have enough BLURT to pay the listing fee.
broadcast_error.body_locked: The session is locked. Unlock your password to try again.
broadcast_error.body_bad_password: That password didn't unlock your keystore. Try again.
broadcast_error.body_posting_only: Paying the listing fee in BLURT needs your Active key. {brand} will ask for it when you post — it signs the fee and is never stored on this device. You can also go back and pay in BTC/XMR, or use your free first listing.
broadcast_error.body_recipient_missing: The listing fee couldn't be sent — the treasury account it pays to (@morphit-fees) doesn't seem to exist on Blurt yet. Nothing was paid. If you run this instance, that account needs to be created; otherwise, please report this.
broadcast_error.body_insufficient_rc: Blurt takes a small network fee for this action from your liquid BLURT, and your account could not cover it. Top up a little liquid BLURT (incoming transfers are free) and try again. Nothing was paid.
broadcast_error.body_authority: Blurt rejected the signature on the fee payment — your account's Active key may not match what's on-chain. Nothing was paid. Try signing in again with your 12-word seed or Keyfile.

waiver.heading: Your first order is on us!
waiver.body: Welcome to {brand}! Your first order is a free BLURT buy. We cover the listing fee, and the BLURT you receive funds your future listings at the discounted BLURT rate, lets you vote on Blurt social content for curation rewards, and pays your first BLURT listing fee, which sets aside your 1 BP welcome stake.

fee_method.legend: How would you like to pay the listing fee?
fee_method.waived_hint: One-time benefit for new traders. Applies only to your first buy order.
fee_method.blurt_hint: Pay the listing fee in BLURT. Verified instantly on-chain — no wait for external block explorers.
fee_method.btc_hint: Send the fee to our Bitcoin address, then paste the transaction ID below.
fee_method.xmr_hint: Send the fee from your Monero wallet, then paste the transaction ID and transaction key below.
fee_method.txid_required: Transaction ID or Hash is required.
fee_method.txid_malformed: Transaction ID must be a 64-character hex string.
fee_method.txid_hint: Your order won't appear in the orderbook until the payment is confirmed on its chain.
fee_method.txid_tooltip: The transaction ID from your wallet — a long string of hex characters that proves your payment. Click for details on where to find it.
fee_method.fee_address_heading_btc: Send your BTC fee to this address
fee_method.fee_address_heading_xmr: Send your XMR fee to this address
fee_method.fee_address_chain_pinned: Chain-pinned by {account} — every Morphit instance verifies fees against this address.
fee_method.fee_address_unavailable: This operator hasn't configured a {asset} fee address. Pick BLURT instead, or post your order on a different Morphit instance.
fee_method.blurt_needs_active_key: Needs your Active key. You're signed in with your Posting key — {brand} will ask for your Active key when you post, and nothing you've filled in will be lost.
fee_method.btc_hint_per_order: Post first, then pay: you'll get a Bitcoin address made just for this listing.
fee_method.btc_per_order_body: After you post, you'll see a Bitcoin address made just for this listing and the exact amount to send (about {amount} BTC). Pay it from any Bitcoin wallet and your order goes on the orderbook by itself. No transaction ID to copy.
fee_method.tx_key_tooltip: A 64-character code your Monero wallet shows for every payment you send. It lets anyone check that this one payment reached us, and it cannot move any money. Click for where to find it in your wallet.
fee_method.tx_key_privacy_note: Good to know: this key is published with your listing so every Morphit server can check your payment. It proves this one payment and cannot move any money. Someone who also knows your wallet address could use it to see the change from this payment, so for the most privacy, pay the fee from a wallet address you have not shared with anyone.
fee_method.tx_key_how_to_label: Where do I find the transaction key?
fee_method.tx_key_how_to_cli_body: Type get_tx_key followed by the transaction ID, then copy the key it prints.
fee_method.tx_key_how_to_gui_body: Open Transactions, open the details of the payment, and copy the “Transaction key”.
fee_method.tx_key_how_to_feather_body: In History, right-click the payment, choose “Show details”, then “Copy Tx Secret Key”.
fee_method.tx_key_how_to_cake_body: Tap the payment in your transaction list and copy the “Transaction Key”.
fee_method.tx_key_how_to_monerujo_body: Tap the payment and copy the “TX Key”.
fee_method.tx_key_how_to_other_body: Look in the payment's details for “transaction key”, “tx key” or “tx secret key”. Only the wallet that sent the payment has it — an exchange cannot give it to you. If your wallet does not show it, pay from one of the wallets above, or pay the fee in BLURT.
fee_method.tx_key_hint: Copy it from the same wallet that sent the payment.
fee_method.tx_key_malformed: That is not a transaction key: it is exactly 64 characters, only 0–9 and a–f. A “payment proof” (starting with OutProof) will not work.
fee_method.tx_key_several: Your wallet shows more than one key, which means this payment also went to other addresses. Please send the listing fee in a payment of its own, then use that payment's ID and key.
fee_method.xmr_bound_heading: Send the Monero fee to this listing's own address
